text:
ines: hey all, day 1 question: we're using GitHub Actions + Codespaces. Is there a recommended way to avoid storing hosted/sandbox keys in repo secrets? worried about leaks and also CI flakiness from 429s.
hugo: welcome! :wave: best practice is to avoid long-lived tokens in repo secrets. Two safe patterns: 1) GitHub OIDC -> our token broker (recommended). 2) ephemeral tokens minted via internal service and injected at runtime.
nines: OIDC -> token broker? how does that flow look?
devex-bot: docs: https://internal.redwood.devex/oidc-broker. Flow: Actions/Codespaces request OIDC token from GitHub, your broker (internal service) validates the OIDC JWT, calls our ephemeral-token API to mint a short-lived RW token scoped for the repo/job, and returns it to the runner. No keys stored in repo.
maya: practical tip: scope tokens to minimal privileges and TTL ~15m for Actions, ~2h for interactive Codespaces. Also add a quota-gating step in CI that calls GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account/limits or checks X-RateLimit-Remaining before running heavy e2e tests. If remaining low, skip heavy tests instead of failing.
ops: small GitHub Actions snippet for OIDC + broker (very condensed):
```
- name: Request RW token
  id: rw
  run: |
    TOKEN=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ steps.acquire_jwt.outputs.oidc }}" https://internal.auth/broker/issue?repo=${{ github.repository }})
    echo "RW_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_ENV
- name: Check quota
  run: |
    REMAIN=$(curl -sI -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | grep -Fi X-RateLimit-Remaining | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d '\\r')
    if [ -z "$REMAIN" ] || [ "$REMAIN" -lt 50 ]; then echo "skip heavy e2e: low quota ($REMAIN)"; exit 0; fi
```
nines: sweet. For Codespaces can we use the same broker?
hugo: yes. Codespaces can call the broker after SSO login. If you need per-dev permissions, broker issues tokens scoped to user identity.
devex-bot: reminder: to request larger CI/demo quota, open https://internal.redwood.devex/requests/keys with team, window, concurrency, and whether streaming is required. Mark as "OIDC/broker" if you plan to use the broker.
nines: thanks folks, i'll wire up the broker and add the quota gate to our workflows. helps a lot :smile:
